agentCan: Drive the Setup UI end-to-end with an authenticated admin session (toggle, app creation, scopes, policies)
Generate the authorize/token URL pair and implement the OAuth flow in your codebase
Run pre-scans (e.g. code analyzers) before any AppExchange submission

approval.trigger: None for private integrations. The AppExchange Security Review is triggered ONLY if you list on AppExchange ($999 per attempt for paid apps, free for free apps; staged estimates imply ~6-10 weeks per cycle, not officially published).

blockers.detail: Each customer connects their own Salesforce org. If their admin disables self-authorization or their licenses lack API access, connection fails no matter how perfect your app is. This is the #1 surprise for agent builders used to consumer OAuth providers.
blockers.howToClear: Document the admin-side prerequisites for customers; offer the 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized' policy as the enterprise-friendly alternative.
blockers.title: Your users' org admins are the real gatekeepers

blockers.detail: The callback URL registered on the app must exactly match the redirect_uri sent at runtime, or authorization fails.
blockers.howToClear: Register every environment's URI (dev, staging, prod) up front.
blockers.title: Redirect URI must match exactly

blockers.detail: Salesforce sends a verification code to the contact email before showing the consumer secret.
blockers.howToClear: Use an email the team controls; an agent with inbox access can complete this step.
blockers.title: Consumer-secret reveal needs your email

sources.label: Dev docs: External Client Apps recommended from Spring '26
Dev blog: preparing for AppExchange security review ($999/attempt)

tested: Read-only verification: every step above was checked against current Salesforce Help, developer docs, and Trailhead pages (no org was created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Whether new orgs must contact Salesforce Support before creating connected apps (one developer guide says so; current Help docs show the self-serve toggle). Treated as possibly context-specific.
No official end-to-end AppExchange review timeline is published; staged estimates (~6-10 weeks/cycle) are third-party.
The docs never explicitly state 'private integrations need no approval'; it follows from the review being listing-triggered.

alternatives: External Client App (Salesforce's recommended path for new integrations from Spring '26)
flavor.why: A Connected App is the documented, universally supported way to get a consumer key/secret pair and let users authorize your agent against any Salesforce org. External Client Apps are Salesforce's direction of travel for ISVs, but add packaging complexity you don't need for a first integration.

humanMust: Sign up for the org, verify email, complete admin login + MFA
Enter the emailed verification code to reveal the consumer secret
Decide the callback URL and the minimal scope set
Each customer's admin must allow self-authorization / API access on their side
name: Salesforce
nuances: No per-user cap and no 'development mode' on private integrations, unlike Spotify.
Salesforce is steering new work toward External Client Apps; Connected Apps remain fully supported but creation now sits behind the 'Allow creation' toggle.
If you later use the JWT bearer flow for server-to-server calls, scopes come from the Permitted Users policy, not the request.

AppExchange listing is a separate, much bigger project: partner enrollment, managed package, security hardening, and a review with real rejection risk (top failure: CRUD/FLS violations in Apex). Budget months, not days.
prerequisites: A Salesforce org where you are an admin (free Developer Edition works)
My Domain deployed in that org (OAuth requires it)
A contact email you control (used for consumer-secret verification)
Your agent's OAuth redirect URI and the scopes you need

steps.detail: Sign up for a free Developer Edition org and verify your email. You need admin rights even in your own org.
steps.title: Get an org with admin rights

steps.detail: In Setup, Quick Find 'External Client Apps' > Settings, turn on 'Allow creation of connected apps'. Note: one Salesforce developer guide suggests new orgs may need to contact Support first; current Help docs still show this self-serve toggle. If the toggle is missing, contact Support.
steps.title: Enable connected-app creation

steps.detail: New Connected App: give it a unique name, keep the auto-derived API name, add your contact email (required), an optional description, and logo/icon URLs (they render on the Salesforce-hosted consent screen, worth doing before customers see it).
steps.title: Create the connected app

steps.detail: Under API (Enable OAuth Settings), check 'Enable OAuth Settings' and enter your Callback URL (your agent's redirect URI; it must match exactly at runtime). Select minimal scopes: api, refresh_token/offline_access, web, plus openid/id/email/profile for identity. Avoid 'full' unless you truly need it; over-broad scopes show on the consent screen and hurt under review.
steps.title: Enable OAuth and choose scopes

steps.detail: The consumer key (client_id) shows immediately. Click Manage Consumer Details to reveal the consumer secret (client_secret): Salesforce emails you a verification code you must enter. Keep the secret server-side.
steps.title: Retrieve the consumer key and secret

steps.detail: Manage > Edit Policies: leave Permitted Users as 'All users may self-authorize' so your users can connect without their admin pre-approving each person (you can tighten this later for enterprise customers).
steps.title: Set OAuth policies

steps.detail: Wait a few minutes for the consumer key to propagate across Salesforce before the first token request, or you will mistake propagation delay for a broken setup. Then run the authorization-code flow against login.salesforce.com (or test.salesforce.com for sandboxes).
steps.title: Wait for propagation, then test

tagline: Let users connect their Salesforce orgs to your agent. No approval needed for private integrations; the heavyweight review only appears if you list on AppExchange.

time.total: Under 2 hours, account to working OAuth
time.waiting: A few minutes (consumer-key propagation, stated in docs)
